# Austerlitz Command Map — Changelog

## 2026-10 · Decision 213 (b): the Russian Guard's strengths from Duffy's page (its own PR)

**Status: done on `claude/magical-rubin-vahnny` (draft PR), for review. The build changed: `austerlitz-command-map.html` @@SIZE@@ bytes,
md5 `@@MD5@@` (PR #57's build: 2,198,549 bytes, `fdc25e82...`).** Begun from `main` at `8e3278e` (PR #57 merged). On 21 October 2026 the
owner sent a photograph of Duffy, *Austerlitz 1805*, pp. 184-185 ("Is this what you're looking for?"), then: "Go with 213 (b) and apply it as
its own small PR." A data task (guarded declarations), with its evidence.

**The reading (register entry S5.7, now on the page image).** Read by the lead on zoomed crops of the owner's photograph (kept outside the
repository: a work in copyright; the passage is quoted in the register): the heading "Reserve, Russian Imperial Guard, Grand Duke Constantine
(10,530, 40 pieces)"; the Izmailovsky 2 bns. 1,000, the Semenovsky 2 bns. 1,400, the Preobrazhensky 2 bns. 1,500, the Guard jägers 1 bn. 530, a
"Guard Gr.R. (in reserve)" 3 bns. 2,300; the Chevalier Garde 5 sqs. 800, the Gardes du Corps 5 sqs. 1,000, the Life Guard Hussars 5 sqs. 800,
the Life Guard Cossacks 2 sqs. 300; pioneers 1 coy. 100; the table ends there. So the pairing PR #57 inferred from the OCR is the page's, and
its alternative explanation (a horse row lost in the OCR, which would have kept the map's 3,700) is refuted: the rows sum to 9,730, and 800 of
the heading's 10,530 is in none of them. The map's 3,700 horse equals 10,530 less 6,730 and 100: a subtraction, not Duffy's figure.

**What changed (was, is, why):**
- `FORMATIONS.rg_inf.strength`: was 6,730; is 4,430, the seven battalions with the Tsesarevich (Duffy's rows: 1,000, 1,400, 1,500, 530).
  Why: the map's Guard infantry is the infantry that fought (its note and track); Duffy's 6,730 adds the grenadier regiment "in reserve",
  which Sokolov (S5.6) puts in Maliutin's separate column.
- `FORMATIONS.rg_inf.strengthNote`: begins "4,430: the seven battalions …", gives Duffy's 6,730 with the reserve regiment's 2,300 not drawn and
  Smith as cited, not read; the rest (the commander) as it was. Its claim, "attributed", rehashed and resting on S5.7 as well.
- `COMPOSITION.rg_inf` (`appearance.js`): the Life Grenadiers' three battalions (`ru_gren`, Schönhals p. 178) taken out; its note says why
  ("not drawn in this formation: 'in reserve' in Duffy, in Maliutin's separate column in Sokolov"). The formation now draws the six Guard
  battalions and the jägers' one.
- `FORMATIONS.rg_cav.strength`: was 3,700; is 2,900, Duffy's four rows, the same four as Schönhals's table that the dress table already
  read (800, 1,000, 800, 300): the map's own composition summed to 2,900 while the strength said 3,700. Its note begins "2,900 horse: Duffy's
  rows …", Smith cited, not read; the rest as it was. Its claim rehashed, resting on S5.7 as well.
- `FORMATIONS.constantine.strengthNote`: was "Duffy and Smith give 6,730 infantry, 3,700 horse, 100 pioneers and 40 guns. Narrative accounts
  often give about 8,500"; is Duffy's heading and rows, the 800 in no row, what the map draws, Smith cited, not read, and the 8,500 sentence
  kept. Its strength stays 10,500 (Duffy's 10,530). It has no claim of its own (unchecked, as before: the 8,500 sentence has no reading).
- `APPEARANCE_SOURCES.duffy1977` (the one table of works read): added, so the claims can cite it.
- `STATEMENT_CLAIMS`: the two notes' claims as above; `rg_inf.commander`'s note no longer says S5.7 is on the text layer.
- `test.js`: the order-of-battle values `rg_inf` 4,430 and `rg_cav` 2,900 (they pin the data, so they follow it).
- **A warning acknowledged, not a check loosened:** the corps declares 10,500 and its two formations now sum to 7,330, past `test.js`'s 30% and
  `redteam.js`'s 25% warnings. The gap is the source's own (the reserve regiment's 2,300, the pioneers' 100 and Duffy's 800 in no row), so each
  warning is acknowledged by its exact text in `KNOWN_WARN` with that reason and this record; the error rule (children never above the
  parent) is unchanged and holds.

**What was not changed:** the Guard's 40 guns; the knowledge model and the tracks (no time or place moved); Smith (still not read, S5.8).

**Verified:** @@VERIFIED@@

**Uncertain, historical:** what Duffy's 800 are; whether "Guard Gr.R." is the Life Grenadier regiment (an inference from Sokolov); Smith's
figures. **Implementation:** the Life Grenadiers are not drawn (no formation of the map is theirs; a formation for them would need a track,
which no source read gives).

**Decision 211 (b): Duffy and Smith read first (no data change).** Duffy, *Austerlitz 1805* (1977), lends on archive.org; its page images and
text are not open from here, so it was read through archive.org's public full-text search (OCR snippets), its appendix's header and strength
row found again by the lead: register entry S5.7 (text layer only, grade C). The OCR gives the page's second column as seven names, then
seven strengths; as the reader pairs them in order (not seen on a page), Duffy's 6,730 would be the three Guard regiments (1,000, 1,400,
1,500), the jägers (530) and a three-battalion "Guard Gr.R. (in reserve)" (2,300): the seven battalions with the Tsesarevich 4,430. His horse
rows as paired sum to 2,900 against the 3,700 the map credits to Duffy and Smith (`rg_cav`); but the map's corps note (6,730, 3,700 and 100)
sums to his 10,530 exactly, and the 800 left over is exactly 3,700 less 2,900: the text layer is consistent with the map's 3,700 if one horse
row was lost in the OCR or the pairing. Smith (1998) could not be read (S5.8, a negative: no copy on archive.org or Open Library; Google Books' quota spent). A reading on the
text layer carries no claim (`test.js`; the register's rule), so the strengths stay, and the choice is owner question 213 (recommended: read
Duffy's pp. 184-185 on the page first).

  31st Bulletin); the 32nd Bulletin, dated 6 December, has Prince Johann of Liechtenstein come to the Emperor at the castle here and conclude
  it with Marshal Berthier." (worded so after the group's review: the Bulletin puts Liechtenstein's visit at the castle, and its sentence on

**Question 187: the claims on screen, as the owner chose ("Index + tags").** Decision 187 recommended (i) one vocabulary, (ii) an index in
the sources sheet first, then a button at the end of the drawer dossiers, each measured, (iii) the framing statements "interpretation" by
class and (iv) the formation dossier's section tags following their statements, with (ii). Its record gives no words or layout, so the
owner was asked how far to take it and chose (i), (ii)'s index alone, (iii) and (iv); the drawer button is question 203.
- *(i) One vocabulary.* `CLAIM_WORDS` (narrative.js) is the vocabulary of the statements' claims, shown now in the index and the tags.
  The three other vocabularies keep their keys; a label takes `CLAIM_WORDS`'s word only where it says the same thing: `SRC_LABEL.inf`
  (app.js, the Command tab) was "INFERRED", is "THIS MAP'S READING" (`CLAIM_WORDS.interpretation`). `CLAIM.disputed.label` (data.js, the
  event pill) was changed from "Disputed" to "The sources disagree" in `c1a000f` and restored after the review: an event's "disputed" also
  covers one source against this map's hour (davout-resumes) and no account's hour against the map's own texts (kamensky), where "the
  sources disagree" overclaims; `CLAIM_WORDS.disputed` requires two sides from two sources, `EVENTS[].claim` does not. Kept, because they
  say more or less than the claim word: `CLAIM.fact` "Fact" ("Attested in the standard
  accounts", not "a source read here"), `CLAIM.est`, `CLAIM.recon`, `CLAIM.disputed`, `SRC_LABEL.doc` "DOCUMENTED" and `.anec` "ANECDOTE" (no Command row is
  checked against a reading by them, so "Read in a source" or "As a source tells it" would overclaim), and `CONF_TEXT.A` (a position's grade,
  not a statement's claim).
- *(ii) The index* (app.js `claimsIndex`, `refLabel`): a section "The statements' claims" in the sources sheet, after the works read: each
  claim word with its definition and its count; the claimed statements listed under it, each by where it is in a visitor's words
  (an event, a phase's line, a formation at a phase, a place, a theme, a tour stop, a Command row, a plan, this sheet) and the works it
  rests on with their locators; the framing classes named with their reasons; "Not yet checked" for every other statement. Read from
  narrative.js alone (no quotation in the build). Measured: check:contrast (the sources sheet is one of its states) and the full
  check:visual at the part's end.
- *(iii) The framing statements by class*: `CLAIM_BY_CLASS` (narrative.js, new, guarded in check:data's group "narrative claims"): every phase
  title, track objective and act line "interpretation", each class with the pattern of its refs and its reason, unless the statement has an
  entry of its own (one act line has). 75 statements so (10 phase titles, 61 track objectives, 4 act lines). Event names, which the
  option put to the owner on 17 October also listed (questions.md's text says "the framing statements" only), are not classed (question
  204): an event's name states the event, whose claim is the event's own (`EVENTS[].claim`,
  shown in its pill), so "This map's reading" would understate a documented event and overstate nothing it adds; recorded here for the
  owner. test.js holds each class to `tools/step4/statements.js`'s classes (its pattern matches that class's refs exactly), its claim one
  that needs no reading (never fact, attributed, disputed or uncertain), and counts them; the inventory shows "interpretation (by class)".
- *(iv) The formation dossier's tags* (app.js `stmtClaim`, `claimTag`): each narrative statement the dossier shows carries its claim's word
  after it: the commander, the composition, the note on the figures, the act before, now and next, the objective, the role, the outcome and
  the note; a statement without a claim "Not yet checked". "What it was doing" and "Why it was there", made of statements alone, lose their
  section tags ("reconstruction", "record"); the sections that hold data rows (Who, How many, Where, Its day, Dress) keep theirs. The tag is
  the layer tag's plate (`.ltag.claim`, style.css), not wrapped inside itself.
- runtime-test.js (new check): in every formation's dossier at five clocks, each claim tag names a live narrative statement with its own
  claim, else its class's, else "unchecked", in `CLAIM_WORDS`'s word, and each statement shown carries one (1,257 tags in 200 dossiers:
  unchecked 883, interpretation 131, disputed 135, attributed 103, derived 5); every one of the 704 statements has a place in the index's
  words; every claimed statement is listed in the index with its kind's count.

**Question 196 (b): a formation waiting at an anchor is graded by that anchor.** As recommended: (b), in its fuller form, which covers
kienmayer@7 too. `confAt` (app.js, a declaration of check:data's "movement, strength and confidence model") graded a formation by the phase
the clock is in, so while it still stood at an anchor waiting for a leg that begins later in the phase it took the next anchor's grade. Was:
between two anchors the weaker one's, else the current phase's; is: before its next leg begins (`legAt`'s `u` 0 with a next anchor) the
anchor it stands at, graded as that anchor is (`stateAt` of its phase); between two anchors and at an anchor as before. The cases this
changes over the day (every minute, every leaf formation, from the model): gqg 11:15-12:00 (A -> B: the headquarters waits at the Zuran
point, gqg@0, B since step 4's K8, until gqg@6's departure at 12:00), friant at 09:00 (one minute, A -> B: at the Goldbach anchor, friant@1,
B, before the leg to the retaking begins) and kienmayer at 14:30 (one minute, A -> B). The dispatch's text already took the earlier phase's
(`waitingFor`) for gqg; it is unchanged. What draws on `confAt` follows: the position mark on the ground, the name's badge, the dossier's
pill and grade. Measured: `opening-4` (14:30) with `harness.js --only` against the final part-A run: no difference in drops, dropped ids,
unobstructed fractions or timeline height; the full check:visual at the part's end. check:data's changed declaration: `confAt`.

  Savary the Russians beginning to debouch on Legrand about seven, Legrand attacked soon after (`savary1828.p204-207`); Stutterheim the
  hussars forward to reconnoitre between seven and eight (`stut1806de.p49-52.telnitz`); the Chevalier Guard's history the eighth hour
  (`kavalergard1851.p56.eighth-hour`, not independent of Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky); Davout Telnitz under vigorous attack by about eight (a
  bound, `davout1885.p202-204.report-26dec`): hours within the hour that disagree, as augezd's half hour does.
- `sokolnitz` 08:00, A -> B. Przybyszewski's column in action from eight (`kutuzov1951.p269-270.przybyszewski`) and Buxhowden's II Column
  coming down at eight toward Sokolnitz (`kutuzov1951.p241-242.buxhowden`), against Davout's "not yet attacked" about eight
  (`davout1885.p202-204.report-26dec`), Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's Langeron engaging at half past eight (`md1844.p179.half-past-eight~C1.c4`)
  and Schönhals's III Column reaching Sokolnitz only after the Pratzen attack began (`schoenhals1873.p160.half-past-seven`).
- `face-about` 09:15, A -> C. No reading gives the hour of Kutuzov's order; the sequence only: the French columns seen and moving about nine
  (`stut.p60-61.nine-pratzen`, `schoenhals1873.p159-161.nine`), the 4th Column met as it left (`kutuzov1951.p230.miloradovich-eight`).
- `pratzeberg` 11:00, A -> B. Ségur has everything succeeded and the Russian centre pierced toward eleven (`segur1873.p467-469.noon-one`);
  Stutterheim's and Schönhals's about two hours from about nine make about eleven only by addition (`stut.p66.two-hours`,
  `schoenhals1873.p162-163.two-hours`); Thiebault has three hours (`thieb.p469.trois-heures`); the 30th Bulletin the whole Allied left cut
  off within the first hour (`corr11.9541.p451.instant`); and the Pratzen chapter calls 11:00 the map's ("on this map the plateau is French
  from end to end by about 11:00").
- `davout-resumes` 12:30, A -> B. Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Napoleon order Davout against the first three columns at one in the afternoon
  (`md1844.p196.one-oclock`), half an hour after the map's 12:30 (`cfcf1b2` graded it C, its search having missed this reading, whose
  register entry names other formations; the review found it).
- `sokolnitz-falls` 14:00, A -> B. No reading dates the fall itself, but the readings' bounds disagree with 14:00: Przybyszewski's men fought
  from eight until four by his report (`kutuzov1951.p269-270.przybyszewski`), Thiebault was wounded beyond the castle about three
  (`thieb.p465-466.three-pm`), Buxhowden had word of the other columns' withdrawal in the second hour after noon
  (`kutuzov1951.p241-242.buxhowden`), Stutterheim the fight decided about two (`stut.p77-79.two-four`).
- `augezd` 14:30, A -> B. Vandamme's division entering Augezd towards two by its aide Vincent, as Thiebault reports him (`thieb.p508.augezd-
  two`), and Stutterheim's "about 2" when Vandamme's division finished the fight (`stut.p77-79.two-four`): half an hour earlier than the map's
  14:30 for taking the height. (Schönhals's left wing past "dieses Defilé" by half past two, `schoenhals1873.p167-169.oudinot`, is the dam by
  Satschan, as the source skeptic corrected, C2.26: a weaker bound.)

  09:30, graded A (`davout1885.p202-204.report-26dec`, read on page images; Schönhals's and Stutterheim's attack about nine agree), the one event graded A.

when Blasowitz fell; when Napoleon took post on the Zuran; when Bernadotte's corps, Drouet's division with it, crossed the Goldbach; how many guns stood by the chapel of St Anthony, and whose; how many men drowned in the meres; how Suchet's and Caffarelli's divisions were numbered on the day (Suchet's the 3rd of V Corps in both October returns read, Gazan's the 2nd on 26 October; Caffarelli's, under Bisson on 28 October, the 1st of III Corps); the brigade of Gladkov cited from Duffy and Smith, which no source read names; whether Uvarov's regiments were with Liechtenstein's column or had gone to Bagration the evening before; the numbers of Rivaud's and Drouet's divisions in I Corps, which the October returns give differently; and the hours on which the accounts read disagree with each other or with this map's timing: when the columns left the plateau (at 07:00 as the disposition ordered, the I Column at seven in Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports and so on the map since roadmap step 4, half past six for the left wing in Schönhals, between seven and eight in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky; the II and III Columns at 07:30 in Schönhals, the III at 07:00 in Przybyszewski's report and the II coming down at 08:00 in Buxhowden's, but from 04:00 on the map), when Kamensky turned his brigade about (no account read gives the hour; at 09:45 in the event, in the 08:45 phase in his brigade's record), when Rapp's counter-charge went in (by about noon in Schönhals, before one by the order of the Bulletin's narrative, about 13:00 in Rapp's and Ségur's memoirs; from 11:15 on the map), when Friant's division left Raigern (at 05:00, or between 05:30 and 06:00, in Davout's two reports, about 06:00 in Sokolov; from 04:00 on the map), when its leading brigade reached the Goldbach (about 09:00 in Stutterheim and the Moniteur's remarks of 1806; 08:00 on the map), when it retook Telnitz (in French hands at 09:30 in Davout's report, then lost again; 08:30 on the map), and when Bagration's corps fell back (with Blasowitz's fall on the map, 11:15; after an attack on its left toward noon in Schönhals). The map keeps its timing for Kamensky's turn, Rapp's charge, the II and III Columns, Friant's division and Bagration's corps. Duffy (1977) and Smith (1998), cited here for strengths, were not read. **The review of `e7f0df1` (K11; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K12's commit).** It extracted both commits, rebuilt the build
(the same md5), ran six light suites and `chronology.js --check` (clean), and confirmed the 11 declarations, an engine changed only in
the blasowitz event's forms, rule L8 for bag@6, tour stop 6's support and its unchanged length (197 characters), the new forms' readings
(Sokolov p. 49; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky p. 255; the Guard jägers in Stutterheim p. 56 and Schönhals p. 164), and that no fixed case stands
in the event's window (11:01-11:41), so smoke, the dossiers' event links and Follow change at no case. Two high, six medium, nine low:
- High: Turas's direction. Through `GEOREF` the Czech register's point for Tuřany lies 2.85 km from where the map draws Turas at a bearing
  of 348 degrees: north-north-west, not west-north-west (the error came from the C6 proposal; the register gives no bearing).
  `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]`, this entry's K11 section and question 191 now say "about 2.8 km north-north-west".
- High: Thiers's coupling of Blasowitz's fall with Bagration's separation stood as fact in the phase-5 lede and `ANALYSIS[#north]`
  ("Bagration is levered away"), against the event's own text and C6.n11 (only Thiers ties them). Both now attribute it to Thiers and give
  Schönhals's later breaking of Bagration's line; bag@6's act says the sequence is this map's.
- Medium: the event's "the Chevalier Guard's history has it occupied without opposition" read as the Russians occupying it; the history
  has the French occupy it "безпрепятственно" (`kavalergard1851.p56-57.malutin-blazovits`). Now "instead has the French occupy it without
  hindrance", its claim side said.
- Medium: "in every account that names its defenders" now names them (the Guard's jägers in Stutterheim, Schönhals and
  Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky); Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's Rivaud is "ordered onto it"; Thiebault's attacker is "the 1st division of Lannes's V
  Corps" (p. 462, "avait disputé", the side no longer "took it"); the claim cites the readings for each (Schönhals p. 164,
  Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky 1846 pp. 255-257, Stutterheim p. 56, Marbot pp. 259-260).
- Medium: C6.p18's skeptic changes: (a) Marbot's version added (Lannes throws the Russians back from the Santon as far as Blasowitz);
  (c) drawing Rivaud's division alone is named this map's inference in the claim's note; (b) the event's tolWhy is left, being still true.
- Medium: `SOURCE_NOTE.refs[0]` (K11's fix) said every formation's note says where its figure comes from; seven formations have no strength
  note and seven name no source. Now: where a note names a source or gives what the sources read it says so, and a figure without a note is
  this map's.
- Medium: Krug and Bellowitz: the skeptic's default ("position not established") is now in `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]`'s open questions.
- Medium: rg_cav's claim cites the Chevalier Guard's history p. 54 (Kologrivov commanding the Guard cavalry on the march) and is
  "attributed": its readings do not oppose each other.
- Low: (1) the Blasowitz feature's reason: Schönhals breaks Bagration's line after Caffarelli's attack toward noon and d'Hautpoul's charge.
  (2) Above. (3) `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]`'s missing comma. (4) The post house's subtitle: "Posoritz", the map's own name, without "(Pozořice)",
  which no reading gives. (5) "Malyutin" now "Maliutin", as rg_inf's commander; that Maliutin led a separate column on the day (the
  Chevalier Guard's history) while the map has him command the Guard infantry is handed on. (6) The Allied I Column's order says "the Turas
  wood" is the disposition's name, not that the wheel is its words. (7) Three chronology reasons named a removed allowance; bag@6's
  locations are current. (8) K11's checks line said `TOUR` (stops 6 and 9): stop 9's text did not change, only its claim; and "Vare"
  is one spelling in `data.js` only (`appearance.js` keeps "Varé", as it keeps "Thiébault"). (9) `runtime-test.js`'s probe now also holds
  that an explicit claim equal to its grade's brings no note.

how Suchet's and Caffarelli's divisions were numbered on the day (Suchet's the 3rd of V Corps in both October returns read, Gazan's the 2nd on 26 October; Caffarelli's, under Bisson on 28 October, the 1st of III Corps); the brigade of Gladkov cited from Duffy and Smith, which no source read names; whether Uvarov's regiments were with Liechtenstein's column or had gone to Bagration the evening before; the numbers of Rivaud's and Drouet's divisions in I Corps, which the October returns give differently; and the hours on which the accounts read disagree with each other or with this map's timing: when the columns left the plateau (at 07:00 as the disposition ordered, the I Column at seven in Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports and so on the map since roadmap step 4, half past six for the left wing in Schönhals, between seven and eight in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky; the II and III Columns at 07:30 in Schönhals, the III at 07:00 in Przybyszewski's report and the II coming down at 08:00 in Buxhowden's, but from 04:00 on the map), when Kamensky turned his brigade about (no account read gives the hour; 08:00 on the map), when it retook Telnitz (in French hands at 09:30 in Davout's report, then lost again; 08:30 on the map), and when Bagration's corps fell back (with Blasowitz's fall on the map, 11:15; after an attack on its left toward noon in Schönhals). The map keeps its timing for Kamensky's turn, Rapp's charge, the II and III Columns, Friant's division and Bagration's corps. Duffy (1977) and Smith (1998), cited here for strengths, were not read. Kamensky's musketeer regiment is named here as Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky names it, Ryazhsk; the Materialien of 1806 give Ryazan, as this map earlier cited from Duffy, which is kept as the other reading. Two known limits of the terrain model are left as they are rather than reshaped to fit: its stream beds are not downhill at every point (reverse gradients of up to about 10 m within a reach), and from the chapel of St Anthony it does not show the centre of the Satschan pond, although Napoleon is recorded watching the end from there.”; unchecked.

**The review of `69031df` (K10; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K11's commit).** It extracted both commits, rebuilt the build
(the same md5) and ran six light suites (clean) and `chronology.js --check` (0 errors). It confirmed the 11 declarations and the changed
texts listed (the kursk claim in the prose), that no `strength` or `guns` value moved, that the engine changed only in kursk's claim ("est"
defensible under `CLAIM`'s notes), and that the appearance label and the two sources pass. The figures 6,340, 6,380, 23,600 and its breakdown,
7,361, 5,000-6,000, 5,600, 4,600, 3,600 (derived), 21,000, 133 guns, 5,922, forty and forty-five colours and up to 1,600 match their readings. Two
high, four medium, eight low:
- High: Kienmayer's note credited 6,800 to "Duffy and Smith as transcribed here", but the transcription's halves make 6,880 (the final
  audit's arithmetic finding). It now says 6,800 is this map's working figure, not from a source read, and that the transcription made
  6,880; Schönhals's split is derived, and his total line prints 2,440 horses (C5.1); "'about 4,700' ... until roadmap step 4", a changelog
  remark, is gone.

  (about 19 November) and the advance from Olmütz (24 November), as C5.24's skeptic dated them. The row now dates them, and its claim's
  note says that the not knowing, as well as the low estimate, is this map's inference.
- Medium: Schönhals's forty guns are Oudinot's ("10 Grenadier-Bataillone unter Oudinot mit 40 Kanonen", C5.20 as its skeptic limits it):

every account that names its defenders (the Chevalier Guard's history: occupied without opposition); its attackers are disputed (Bernadotte's
corps in Stutterheim, Lannes's division in Thiebault, part of Rivaud's with Caffarelli and Kellermann in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky, Caffarelli's
13e Legere in Sokolov); no source names Bagration in it, and Schönhals separates him later. The event is renamed "The French take Blasowitz

reason is labelled the map's reading after Thiers. bag@6 is now judged against Schönhals's "toward noon" and named a conflict (question 180;

read. The Allied plan's I Column wheels "toward the Turas wood" (the disposition's words). The Posoritz post house's subtitle says it was

**The review of `046b85b` (K9; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K10's commit).** It extracted both commits, rebuilt the build (the
same md5), ran `test.js`, `redteam.js`, `binding-test.js`, `sim-test.js` and `chronology.js --check` (clean). It confirmed the 11 declarations and
40 changed statements listed, and an engine identical but for heightguns@8's claim. The figures quoted (Suchet's 36 guns, 138 horses and three
bodies; Lejeune's more than six thousand; Thiebault's three to four thousand; Schönhals's sixty to a hundred; the proclamation's words; the
first rays; long before day) match their readings. One high, five medium, six low:
- High: the French plan's author said the last orders were given "before dawn on the barrow by Schlapanitz in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky". His
  page has the marshals summoned before dawn and the final orders given once the sun lit the hilltops (`md1844.p177.kurgan-sun`), and the
  sentence opened "The last orders were given at daybreak" as fact before three accounts that disagree. It now reads "The moment of the last
  orders differs: at the first rays of the sun in the 30th Bulletin; in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky once the sun lit the hilltops, the marshals
  having been summoned to the barrow by Schlapanitz before dawn; in Savary only once the attack on the right was pronounced". It adds the
  dispositions' Soult's three divisions beyond the ravine at seven (C4.p5).
- Medium: the Command tab's phase-0 order had the army "stand as disposed behind the Goldbach ... Soult's two divisions in the valley".
  The dispositions order moves for seven, Soult's three divisions beyond the ravine for an advance in echelons (`corr11.p442.soult-0730`).
  It now says so.
- Medium: the ice line said "No source read gives the hour", but Thiebault puts the drowning in the last half hour of the firing, after
  about three (`thieb.p466.ice`). The line now gives both accounts (the claim "disputed"), and dok@8's chronology row records both
  readings.
- Medium: "'la butte' by the road" (gqg@0's act, the Zuran's facts) is an inference from the grenadiers' order, as the skeptic limited it
  (C4.p3); "by the road" is gone.
- Medium: K9's entry said nothing drawn at a fixed case changed. That is wrong: the dispatch draws the phase's lede and lines and the
  formations' acts (app.js `paintDispatch`, `paintChanges`), in the rail's Now tab when docked and as a card over the map below 1080 px. The ten
  cases that draw it, the first-run card or the phase-8 texts were measured on this commit's build (below), and the entries of K5 to K9 rest on that
  measurement for those cases.
- Medium: heightguns' note counted Stutterheim among those placing the fire "from the heights", but he does not say where the guns stood
  (`stut.p74-75.kapelle-teich`). The note now says so, and that by the chapel the sector is documented and the point estimated (decision
  154's grade B, "Position: estimated").
- Low: (7) heightguns@8's "by the chapel of St Anthony (Schönhals)": Schönhals has "auf der Höhe", so the chapel is now this map's inference.
  The phase-8 lede has Napoleon come to the chapel (Schönhals), not watch from it. rg_inf@7 has Ségur's Bernadotte "about to complete" the
  Guard's defeat. (8) C4.p9 is applied: the chapel "lost its roof about the time of the battle", the local tradition of the first cannon shot is
  kept as a tradition (`austerlitzorg2000` registered, a web text), and the dates rest on web texts. C4.p11: Sokolov's note 88 (Alombert and
  Colin, t. 5, p. 297, in a reprint of 2002). Recorded, not done: C4.p8's further sources for the guns (Stutterheim p. 78, Schönhals's guns
  by Tellnitz, Lejeune's "la hauteur"), and C4.p2's row for the Bulletin's "one in the morning", which the extractor does not read (the bare
  word hours, already handed on). (9) `ANALYSIS[#collapse].text` has the ice event's claim. (10) The comments on heightguns' explicit claim in
  `app.js` and `runtime-test.js` now say no track claim in the data differs from its grade. `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s decision-154 basis ("the Újezd
  local history") will be corrected with the step's records at the end. (11) Three language slips mended (a comma splice in guard_inf@6's act, a
  missing verb in the phase-8 lede, "having come"). (12) gqg@0's "Position: documented" beside "taken here to be the Zuran" is question 160's,
  left for K8. (13) The Zuran's Berthier rests on Thiebault p. 456 (`thieb.p456.before-day-reread`), not the Bulletin's battle-array sentence.

**The strengths, the losses, Gladkov, the Allied belief and the Kursk regiment (the plan's A3.17, A5.1-A5.3, A5.5, A5.6, A5.8, A5.9, A5.11,
A5.14; questions 184, 185; K10).** Every working figure and every pin is kept (question 184's default); each note now says where its figure
comes from and what the readings give: Kienmayer 6,800 (Duffy and Smith as transcribed, cited, not read) against 6,340 (Schönhals) and 6,380
(Sokolov); "about 4,700" found in no source read. IV Corps's 23,600 is Sokolov's estimate from the returns of 22 November, the three divisions'
working figures not from a source read; Legrand 7,361 on 22 November (Sokolov) and 5,000-6,000 (Stutterheim); Legrand's brigadiers in Sokolov
and the 28 October situation beside the map's (the pinned words kept). Liechtenstein 5,400 inside the range read (5,600 Schönhals; 4,600
Sokolov and Stutterheim; about 3,600 without Uvarov's regiments, derived); "up to 7,000" found in no source read. The grenadiers' artillery:
Sokolov lists a foot and a horse company, against the note's "no artillery listed". The Guard: about 5,500 (Sokolov's estimate); no return
gives its guns on the day (forty in the Bulletin and Schönhals; 24 of its horse artillery at the meres in Sokolov); "24 guns" had no source.
The losses (question 185's default): the phase-9 lede gives the figures attributed (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's up to 21,000 Russian and 5,922
Austrian; Schönhals's; the official report printed in 1806; Napoleon's forty and forty-five colours; the French reports through Sokolov),
not "usually given as 15,000-16,000 ... about 180 guns and 45 standards" (not found in that form); tour stop 9 gives the range in words.
Gladkov is found in none of the works read; Uvarov's brigadier is Penitsky in Schönhals and Gizhitsky in Sokolov. The Allied staff believed
the French few at Brünn (Stutterheim) and in retreat (Czartoryski, read partly on the text layer). The Kursk regiment: Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky,
Langeron's journal as Sokolov quotes it, and Schönhals name it, its strength engaged and its loss disputed; the kursk event's claim recon ->
est (attested; its hour this map's). The Austrian colours' "used to 1806" is an inference (Dolleczek's next pattern is of 1806): the label
fact -> inference in `appearance.js`. `czartoryski1887` is registered.
The division numbers (question 155, H-11): Suchet's division is the 3rd of V Corps in both French returns of October read and in Sokolov's
order of battle built on the returns of 22 November (none of 2 December), so its designation is "3e Div., V Corps" (was "3e or 2e", the
2nd with no source read); Rivaud's note adds Sokolov's numbering of I Corps (Rivaud the 1st, Drouet the 2nd), the "or" kept in both
designations (the returns disagree). The designation is shown only in the dossier's subtitle.

**The review of `35f550a` (K7; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K9's commit).** It extracted both commits, rebuilt the
build (the same md5), ran `test.js`, `redteam.js`, `binding-test.js`, `sim-test.js` and `chronology.js --check` (clean), confirmed that
`data-invariance.js` lists exactly the entry's ten declarations and the 33 changed statements, and compared the engine (no `tm`, position,
via, moveMin, event clock or phase clock moved; only the two events' claims, guard-broken's forms, `KNOW_OVERRIDE.al` and one Command tag
changed). On screen, `KNOW_OVERRIDE` draws drouet and rivaud as "?" zones under the Allied headquarters' reading in phases 3-5; the contrast
state "eyes-dossier" and the self-test's reason check still pick the same formations. One high, four medium, six low:
- High: "The Guard infantry breaks two French battalions" (the phase-6 lede, `ANALYSIS[#guard]`, rg_inf@6's act) stood under a "disputed"
  claim whose note said it was not checked, and the readings give the two battalions to the Horse Guard. Schönhals has the Life Guard Horse
  cut down a battalion of the 4th and a light battalion of the 24th (`schoenhals1873.p164.guard-blasowitz`). The Bulletin has a battalion of
  the 4th charged by the Russian Guard horse (`corr11_1863.p451.guard-centre-reserve`). The Allied report has two squadrons of the Garde à
  Cheval cut down a whole battalion (`mat1806.p114-118.guardreport`). The Guard infantry's part is Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's: it overthrows
  "les deux premières colonnes" with the bayonet (`mikhailovsky1846.p259.guard-columns`). The three texts now say so, with those readings
  cited; the note no longer says "not checked".
- Medium: Coignet stood only as saying the foot Guard was engaged. His second line is the morning attack on the Pratzen (p. 122), and of the
  Russian Guard's attack he writes "nous croyions notre tour arrivé, mais ils battirent en retraite" (p. 123). The Guard's role and
  guard_inf@6's act now give both, citing `coignet1909.p121-123.guard-followed` and the Bulletin's p. 451.
- Medium: drouet@7's "Savary has the division go back" named a division Savary does not name. It now reads: one of Bernadotte's
  divisions, unnamed, breaks the Russian Guard infantry, then goes back to its morning place. Ségur's Bernadotte left on the plateau is added
  (C3.p9's required change).
- Medium: Schönhals's "about nine" is Friant's renewed attack on the village, not the brigade's arrival. The davout event's why and

**The Zuran, the chapel battery, the ice and the sun (the plan's A4.1-A4.14, texts; questions 154, 160, 186; K9).** No source read names
the Zuran: the orders of 1 December send headquarters to "la butte" by the road, Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Napoleon on "the barrow by
Schlapanitz", and the dispositions call the marshals to his bivouac for half past seven. The headquarters' act, role, the phase-0 line, the
Zuran's facts and story, the Command tab's phase-0 rows and the French plan's author now say so, the identification with the Zuran named as
one; the Bulletin's ride round the posts at one in the morning, Thiebault's "long before day", and the moment of the last orders (the first
rays in the Bulletin, before dawn in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky, once the attack on the right was pronounced in Savary) are attributed. The
deception chapter quotes the proclamation's own words (the enemy, turning his right, will present its flank), the Bulletin's sentence and
Marbot's trap, and labels the map's reading. The chapel battery (question 154): the "Újezd local history" with its 24 guns does not stand
(the town's own text has no battery; the composite is found only on a tourist website); the period sources give the sector, artillery of IV
Corps and the Guard on the height above Augezd (Schönhals; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Napoleon place the Guard artillery there): its act,
its strength note (every count attributed, none at the chapel) and the chapel's facts (completed 1703, closed 1785, roofless about the time
of the battle, reconsecrated 1863, after the town's account; "burned in 1805" on a tourist website) say so, and heightguns@8's claim is
"est" (Position: estimated; grade B kept, decision 154). The drowning and the drained count (question 186's default): every account kept,
attributed (the Bulletin's twenty thousand; Marbot's thousands; Thiebault's three to four thousand; Lejeune's more than six thousand;
Stutterheim's "some"; Schönhals's sixty to at most a hundred, on the Telnitz priest's word); the count from the drained pond is General
Suchet's report of 16 December 1805 as Sokolov quotes it (36 guns, 138 horses, three bodies; the French text not read), the figures usually
given (38 guns, about 130 horses, two men) kept as not traced. The ice line's hour: no source read gives 15:00 (Schönhals has the left wing
past the Satschan dam by half past two; Thiebault the firing over about half an hour after three). `SOURCE_NOTE.refs[1]` no longer says the
Pratzeberg narrative follows Duffy, who was not read. Registered: `lejeune1895`, `stutterheim1806fr2`, and two web texts read on their text,
`ujezd2025` and `turistika_kaple` (which can carry only "disputed" or "uncertain"). check:chronology: the phase-0 line's half past seven
allowed by name (an order of the evening before); the ice line's half past two cited by dok@8.

the upper bound of the Russian Guard's attack; Bagration's exact line at dawn; the exact place of the Posoritz post house; the true position of Turas; Kologrivov's command, which rests on one source; when Blasowitz fell; when Napoleon took post on the Zuran; when Bernadotte's corps, Drouet's division with it, crossed the Goldbach; how many guns stood by the chapel of St Anthony, and whose; how many men drowned in the meres; how Suchet's and Caffarelli's divisions were numbered on the day (Suchet's the 3rd of V Corps in both October returns read, Gazan's the 2nd on 26 October; Caffarelli's, under Bisson on 28 October, the 1st of III Corps); the brigade of Gladkov cited from Duffy and Smith, which no source read names; whether Uvarov's regiments were with Liechtenstein's column or had gone to Bagration the evening before; the numbers of Rivaud's and Drouet's divisions in I Corps, which the October returns give differently; and the hours on which the accounts read disagree with each other or with this map's timing: when the columns left the plateau (at 07:00 as the disposition ordered, the I Column at seven in Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports and so on the map since roadmap step 4, half past six for the left wing in Schönhals, between seven and eight in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky; the II and III Columns at 07:30 in Schönhals, the III at 07:00 in Przybyszewski's report and the II coming down at 08:00 in Buxhowden's, but from 04:00 on the map), when Kamensky turned his brigade about (no account read gives the hour; at 09:45 in the event, in the 08:45 phase in his brigade's record), when Rapp's counter-charge went in (by about noon in Schönhals, before one by the order of the Bulletin's narrative, about 13:00 in Rapp's and Ségur's memoirs; from 11:15 on the map), when Friant's division left Raigern (at 05:00, or between 05:30 and 06:00, in Davout's two reports, about 06:00 in Sokolov; from 04:00 on the map), when its leading brigade reached the Goldbach (about 09:00 in Stutterheim, Schönhals and the Moniteur's remarks of 1806; 08:00 on the map) and when it retook Telnitz (in French hands at 09:30 in Davout's report, then lost again; 08:30 on the map). The map keeps its timing for Kamensky's turn, Rapp's charge, the II and III Columns and Friant's division. Duffy (1977) and Smith (1998), cited here for strengths, were not read. Kamensky's musketeer regiment is named here as Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky names it, Ryazhsk; the Materialien of 1806 give Ryazan, as this map earlier cited from Duffy, which is kept as the other reading. Two known limits of the terrain model are left as they are rather than reshaped to fit: its stream beds are not downhill at every point (reverse gradients of up to about 10 m within a reach), and from the chapel of St Anthony it does not show the centre of the Satschan pond, although Napoleon is recorded watching the end from there.”; **The review of `ffb0ac4` (K6; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K7's commit).** It compared the two commits' data (no `tm`,
position, departure, arrival, event clock or phase clock moved; only the stated grades and claims changed), confirmed that the committed build
is the commit's and that `data-invariance.js` lists exactly the declarations the entry lists, and ran `test.js`, `redteam.js`,
`binding-test.js` and `chronology.js --check` (clean). Two high, three medium, eight low:
- High: the phase-1 line on Friant's leading brigade used Davout's "about eight" as a side of the arrival hour. Davout has only word of the
  attack reach him on the march about eight, and gives no hour for the arrival (C1.33, C2.15). The line now says the hour on the timeline is
  this map's: Stutterheim and the Moniteur's remarks have Friant's men come up about nine, and Schönhals has them attack about nine
  (`schoenhals1873.p157-159.departure`). The davout event's why says the same, and `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]` names the Goldbach hour.
  check:chronology allows its 09:00 by name: no anchor dates the arrival, and friant@2 judges the village held at 09:30.
- High: the davout and telnitz-retaken events were claimed "est". `CLAIM.est` reads "the figure or frontage shown is an estimate", and
  `CLAIM.disputed` describes this case: the accounts disagree with this map's timing, which it keeps. Both are now "disputed", cf B, each with
  a dispute naming both hours (07:45 to 08:15 on the map against about 09:00; 08:30 on the map against 09:30 in Davout and about 09:00 in
  Schönhals and Stutterheim). Their map labels and markers now carry "(hour disputed)", like the other named conflicts' events. The dispute
  sentences' hours are cited by friant@2 (09:30) or allowed by name with their reasons. The telnitz-retaken why's claim is "disputed" with
  the same four readings.
- Medium: the end of the day's "victory decided at one" cited `corr11.9541.p451`, the step-2 entry whose quote leaves that sentence out. It
  now cites `corr11.9541.p451.instant` (C2.6, "A une heure après midi la victoire était décidée"), in `EVENTS[#end].dispute` and
  `PHASES[#8].events[2]`.
- Medium: three texts on the 4th Column said "in Russian accounts until the Tsar ordered it forward" and "Kutuzov's reluctance to leave the
  heights". No reading in either register says so: Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Kutuzov stand still though the disposition ordered him
  forward (`md1844.p181.ninth-hour`). `ANALYSIS[#pratzen].text`, `PLANS.al.cost` and `EVENTS[#counter-march].why` now say what he says.
  The Allied plan's cost no longer gives Schönhals an order (he has the column leave half an hour later) and attributes the hold-up.
  Recorded, not changed: the same story stands in the kollo note, the Kollowrat dossier's story and the Allied headquarters' phase-3 act,
  attributed there to the Russian Biographical Dictionary (1903), which no step-4 reader read; handed on.
- Medium: the phase-2 lede put Telnitz retaken and lost in the 08:00-08:45 phase on Davout's word. It now names Davout's half past nine,
  and says the map shows it in this phase (cited by friant@2).
- Low: (6) three claim notes put the loss in the fog on p. 203's cut margin; it is on p. 204, read on the page image. (7) "retaken at half past
  nine" is now "in French hands at half past nine" (Davout's "à neuf heures et demie le village était en notre pouvoir": at, not by) in
  friant@2's note, the chronology row and `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]`, whose list loses a stray "and". (8) The Raigern departure is "disputed": Davout's two
  reports and Sokolov's about six (`sokolov2006.p19-61`), as the source skeptic's required change (f) asked. (9) Sokolov's locators carry

stood at dawn (Savary's second line, Stutterheim's Girzikowitz, Marbot's ravine, Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's crossing the evening before) is a

when Blasowitz fell; when Napoleon took post on the Zuran; when Bernadotte's corps, Drouet's division with it, crossed the Goldbach; how many guns stood by the chapel of St Anthony, and whose; how many men drowned in the meres; how Suchet's and Caffarelli's divisions were numbered on the day (Suchet's the 3rd of V Corps in both October returns read, Gazan's the 2nd on 26 October; Caffarelli's, under Bisson on 28 October, the 1st of III Corps); the brigade of Gladkov cited from Duffy and Smith, which no source read names; whether Uvarov's regiments were with Liechtenstein's column or had gone to Bagration the evening before; the numbers of Rivaud's and Drouet's divisions in I Corps, which the October returns give differently; and the hours on which the accounts read disagree with each other or with this map's timing: when the columns left the plateau (at 07:00 as the disposition ordered, the I Column at seven in Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports and so on the map since roadmap step 4, half past six for the left wing in Schönhals, between seven and eight in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky; the II and III Columns at 07:30 in Schönhals, the III at 07:00 in Przybyszewski's report and the II coming down at 08:00 in Buxhowden's, but from 04:00 on the map), when Kamensky turned his brigade about (no account read gives the hour; at 09:45 in the event, in the 08:45 phase in his brigade's record), and when Rapp's counter-charge went in (by about noon in Schönhals, before one by the order of the Bulletin's narrative, about 13:00 in Rapp's and Ségur's memoirs; from 11:15 on the map), when Friant's division left Raigern (at 05:00, or between 05:30 and 06:00, in Davout's two reports; from 04:00 on the map) and when it retook Telnitz (at 09:30 in Davout's report, then lost again; 08:30 on the map). The map keeps its timing for Kamensky's turn, Rapp's charge, the II and III Columns and Friant's division. Duffy (1977) and Smith (1998), cited here for strengths, were not read. Kamensky's musketeer regiment is named here as Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky names it, Ryazhsk; the Materialien of 1806 give Ryazan, as this map earlier cited from Duffy, which is kept as the other reading. Two known limits of the terrain model are left as they are rather than reshaped to fit: its stream beds are not downhill at every point (reverse gradients of up to about 10 m within a reach), and from the chapel of St Anthony it does not show the centre of the Satschan pond, although Napoleon is recorded watching the end from there.”; **The review of `aa561af` (K5; an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K6's commit).** It rebuilt the commit (the same md5), ran
`test.js`, `redteam.js`, `sim-test.js` and `chronology.js --check` (clean), and compared the engine before and after (only the stated grades
changed; no departure, arrival, position or event clock moved). One high, two medium and five low:
- High: the 4th Column "ordered to move at eight (Schönhals)" was wrong: the disposition sets every column off at seven (Schönhals says so
  too); "toward eight" is Stutterheim's (the 4th Column ordered off late, to give the left wing's columns time), and Schönhals's half hour is
  the same intent; the delay is Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's (the cavalry at the set hour, then Kutuzov standing still). The chapter on the
  Pratzen, the counter-march event and the Allied plan's cost now say so, their claims "disputed" with the four readings.
- Medium: the end of the day's claims cited only Bagration's retreat and Sokolov: they now cite the readings that date the end of the firing
  (the Allied report's north quiet from three, Thiebault's half an hour after three, Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky's last shots between five and
  six, the Bulletin's victory decided at one), and the end's dispute and the phase-8 line name them. The allowance of the end's 18:00
  described a retreat on Austerlitz the map does not draw: bag@9, the last anchor, lies on the Rausnitz road, where Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky
  has Bagration at dusk; the reason says so (question 180 (c)), and the end's new 15:00 is allowed by name.
- Low: the guard-attack event's claim cites Rapp, Ségur and Schönhals for its hours; the decision's claims add Schönhals's order about nine;
  "Savary" was the sources note's alone (this entry's wording); the timing grades made consistent with `TIMING_TEXT` (an hour inside the
  sources' range, or from a sequence, is C): the soult and blasowitz events B -> C, like the climbs and bag@6 (the ice keeps B, its range
  named: Schönhals's half past two, Thiebault's half an hour after three); c_gren@8 cites Thiebault; the Blasowitz line names the order of
  its fall by account (during the cavalry fights in Schönhals, after the 3rd and 4th Columns were thrown back in the Allied report). K5's
  check:visual was not run (no drawn label changed at a case clock); its check:selftest and check:contrast ran after the commit.

**Friant at the Goldbach and Telnitz retaken (the plan's A2.3; question 177's default; K6).** Davout's report of 26 December (no. 127, read
on the page images, p. 203's cut margin restored in part from the text layer) has word of the attack on Telnitz reach him on the march about eight and the village "à neuf heures et demie" in French
hands, then lost again when a French regiment, not recognising Heudelet's brigade in the fog, fired on it; Stutterheim and the Moniteur's
remarks of 1806 have Friant's 4,000 come up about nine; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky after Telnitz had fallen; Davout's two reports send the
division from Raigern at five (2 December) or between half past five and six (26 December). The engine is kept (question 177's default):
the texts say what the sources say and that the hours on the timeline are this map's; "then withdraws behind the stream" and "a deliberate
step back" (contradicted) are gone; the telnitz-retaken event's name is shorter ("Friant retakes Telnitz, then loses it again"), its claim
fact -> est and timing A -> B. The march's figures: about 115 km in under two days (Sokolov) and thirty-six leagues in forty-eight hours
(Thiers), each attributed; this map's earlier "113 km in 40-46 hours" has no source read and is kept, so labelled, only in the Vienna road's
facts. check:chronology: friant@1 (the departure from Raigern) and friant@2 (Telnitz retaken) now judge the sources' hours and are named
conflicts (`CONFLICTS`), the map's 04:00, 08:00 and 08:30 allowed by name; `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]` names the two hours (rule L8).

kamensky@3, kamensky@4, lang@1, prz@1); check:data against the step-2 reference, no declaration added to the step's changed list. The

  rows now judge 07:30-08:00 and 07:00-07:30 (still early, still named), and the event's dispute and `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]` name those hours.

**The review of `d23df4a` (an independent reviewer, read-only; fixed in K4's commit).** It rebuilt the commit (the same md5), ran `test.js`
and `redteam.js` (clean) and found no high item, four medium and six low:
- Medium: the Augezd note read Stutterheim's night posting as a night march (he has Soult posted by Kobelnitz in the night and attacking
  through Kobelnitz and Puntowitz in the morning): the note and this entry corrected. The phase-8 lede still stated "ran through ground the
  French held" after a colon: now "as running through ground the French held", inside the map's reading. The act line's "is thrown back"
  cited only Stutterheim, who has the Guard retire unpursued: the claim adds the Bulletin's "en déroute" and Ségur, and its note names both
  versions. The Perrot relabel made consistent: the Guard chasseurs' coat and the horse grenadiers' coat (both "like the grenadiers'"), the
  grenadiers' bearskin and the chasseurs' "bonnet" read as bearskin are "inference" with notes; the Guard artillery's coat keeps "fact" with a
  note that the era of Perrot's p. 232 was not established.
- Low: the Old Vineyards' claim note follows the text's "Allied official report"; the Pratzeberg note keeps its first half (placing the
  fight "here" is the map's: Thiebault says "cette partie des hauteurs de Pratzen"); the Command row's height is Schönhals's "auf der Höhe",
  its identification with the height above Augezd the map's reading; question 194 (a) no longer says the uhlan cap and the shabraques are
  drawn by colour, question 189 (c) says deferring amends 136's timing. The Blasowitz event and the north chapter now say Schönhals's
  disorder comes after an attack toward noon: deferred to K11's commit, where the event's text is rewritten.

**The three disputed hours (decision 125 (b); the plan's A1.1-A1.3; question 161; K4).** Step 2 marked three hours on which this map's
own texts disagreed and left them for the published accounts; step 4 read them (register C1):
- *The columns' descent.* The disposition orders all five columns to march at seven (Materialien 1806, pp. 101-106, read on the page images,
  A), and Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports have the I Column leave its camp at seven (Kutuzov, documents, 1951, pp. 241-242, 255-258, A);
  Schönhals has the left wing off at half past six, Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky the first three columns between seven and eight. This settles the
  named conflict dok@1 from the sources: dok@1 now departs at 07:00 (`tm {dep:420, gr:"A", basis:"source"}`; the arrival derived, 07:33), the
  timeline's phase-1 line reads "c. 07:00", the I Column's arrow is derived from its leg (`OVERLAYS` phase 1, `leg:["dok",0,1]`), and dok@1
  leaves `CONFLICTS` and `binding-test.js`'s `UNSETTLED`. dok@2's arrival stays 08:00, so the engine moves the column differently only between
  04:00 and 08:00, where no harness case stands. The II and III Columns keep this map's 04:00 (question 176's default: retiming them moves the
  plateau reading's dawn figures and sim-test's mechanism assertion, which only the owner may replace); their texts say the disposition
  ordered seven, and lang@1 and prz@1 are named conflicts in `check:chronology` (their rows judge the sources' 06:30-07:00 side; the map's 04:00
  allowed by name).
- *Kamensky's turn.* No account read gives the hour, only a sequence (after the French began to climb, before or with Jurczek's attack); the
  accounts differ on who turned the brigade (Kamensky himself in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky after Langeron's report; Langeron in Schönhals;
  Kutuzov in his official report, with Stutterheim's regiments sent by the commander-in-chief; no order of Kutuzov's in his private relation of
  March 1806). The texts say so; the event keeps 09:45 (decision 142; question 178's default) and kamensky@3 and @4 stay named conflicts, now
  internal only.
- *Rapp's counter-charge.* Before one by the order of the narrative in the 30th Bulletin and in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky (an inference: neither
  dates the charge), by about noon in Schönhals, about 13:00 or after in Rapp's own memoirs and Ségur's. guard-broken's claim becomes
  "disputed" with that dispute (question 161, decided in step 2 as "step 4, recorded"); the timeline's "c. 11:45" (this map's own, which no
  source gives) becomes "after 11:15"; guard_cav@6's row now judges the sources' 13:00 side and stays a named conflict; the windows and the
  engine's 11:15 are kept (question 179's default).

  have been); the sources sheet's note on hand-authored arrows likewise; `SOURCE_NOTE.body[5]`'s open question on the three hours now says
  what was read, and that Duffy (1977) and Smith (1998) were not.

**The interpolated position's pill (decision 128 (b); `docs/FINAL_AUDIT.md` H-5; the C7 design skeptic's I5).** A formation's claim pill
read "Position: documented" wherever its grade was A, also where the clock interpolates its position between two documented anchors: the
anchors are documented, the point between them is not (H-5 counted 825 of 2,605 formation-samples; re-counted here on the app's own
functions, 825 of the leaves' 2,636 ten-minute samples).
- `POS_CLAIM` (guarded data in `app.js`): was `{fact:"Position: documented", est:"Position: estimated", recon:"Position: reconstructed"}`;
  is the same with `interp:"Position: interpolated"`. Why: decision 128 (b), H-5. The rule (the smallest, the design skeptic's): the word
  only where the pill would otherwise say "documented" from the grade, no track entry names its own claim, and the position is interpolated;
  B and C interpolations keep "estimated" and "reconstructed", which never overclaimed. The words and the rule are an owner question of this
  step; this is the default meanwhile.
- `app.js`: `posClaimOf(id, cf)` gives the pill's key (a track entry's own claim, else the grade's, "interp" as above); `compactCard` and
  `dossierFormation` draw `posClaimPill(posClaimOf(...))`; `claimOf` is unchanged (the dossier's grade text reads it). The grade pill beside it
  still says "Position A · interpolated". `tokens.js`: `sym.claim.interp` "half" (the estimate's shape; not "derived", which
  `SOURCE_NOTE.layers` keeps for the engine's readings); `style.css`: `.pill.claim-interp` on the pills' plate; `css-test.js` requires it.
- Tests: `runtime-test.js`'s pill assertion (decision 128 (a)) now computes each pill's key itself (from `confAt` and the track's own claims,
  not through `posClaimOf`), requires all four keys at its five clocks (fact 100, est 152, recon 62, interp 86 of 400 pills), and over the
  day's 85 ten-minute clocks checks `posClaimOf` against it for every formation on the field (3,316 samples) and counts the leaves'
  interpolated documented positions (825 of 2,636); shown failing on two mutations (the word removed: the pill throws; the old key: "dok (card)
  at 08:45: the pill's class fact, its key is interp"). A new self-test check, "position pill: the dossier drawn says ...", selects every
  tracked formation on the field at four clocks in Study and reads the drawn pill in `#drawer-body` against a key computed the same way
  (125 dossiers: fact 30, est 44, recon 18, interp 33).
- Checks: npm test, all 9 suites and the height guard; check:chronology 0 errors; check:data "CHANGED data in app.js (roadmap step 2, D-5):
  changed: POS_CLAIM" besides the narrative claims' "not found"; check:selftest 242 checks, all passing, the manifest rewritten from that run
  (241 to 242; added: "position pill: the dossier drawn says “Position: interpolated” where the position is interpolated between documented
  anchors, else its grade's words (roadmap step 4; decision 128 (b), H-5)"; removed: none); check:contrast, run after the commit on its build: 35 states
  reached, 5,517 text elements, 0 below AA, 0 below 10.5 px, 0 font failures, 0 console messages; the six start-up cases pass.
- **The review of `b2fc7b5`, and what changed for it.** No blocking finding. (1) Under the new pill the dossier's grade paragraph still read
  "Position documented in the sources." (`CONF_TEXT.A`), H-5's overclaim in prose: under "Position: interpolated" the paragraph now gives
  `CONF_INTERP` alone (presentation; `CONF_TEXT` and `CONF_INTERP` unchanged). (2) No test fixed that a track's own claim wins over "interp" (no
  datum has both): `runtime-test.js` now gives an interpolated documented leaf a temporary claim and requires it to win, and requires the dossier
  under "Position: interpolated" to say `CONF_INTERP` and not `CONF_TEXT.A`, and a documented position that is not interpolated to say
  `CONF_TEXT.A`; shown failing on the old paragraph ("sthilaire at 04:10: the dossier says "Position documented in the sources." under
  "Position: interpolated""). (3) The count's attribution corrected above (H-5 counted 2,605 samples, not 2,636). (4) The self-test check settles
  its tween after its clock steps (`finishTween`); recorded, not changed: it reads the drawer's card (the full dossier's pill is
  `runtime-test.js`'s), and tracked formations only (aggregates are `runtime-test.js`'s). (5) The explicit-claim scan shared by `claimOf` and
  `posClaimOf` (`explicitClaim`); `compactCard`'s unused `cl` removed. (6) Recorded for the step's records: `docs/VISUAL_SPEC.md` §545 and
  `docs/ROADMAP.md` still describe the three-word pill; "interp" shares the estimate's half shape, told apart by its words.

**The claim model (`narrative.js`; H-6, decision 128 (b)).** A new guarded file after `analysis.js` in `build.py`'s list, as the C7 design
skeptic's review amended the design (its blocking findings B1-B4):
- `CLAIM_WORDS` (new; was: none): the eight claim kinds, each with its word and one-line definition: fact "Read in a source", attributed
  "As a source tells it", disputed "The sources disagree", derived, interpretation "This map's reading", uncertain "Not established", design
  "Design decision", unchecked "Not yet checked". Why: one vocabulary for the per-statement claims, distinct from the event pill's `CLAIM`
  and the Command tab's `SRC_LABEL` (B3); nothing shows it yet (the vocabulary and its visibility are owner questions of this step).
- `STATEMENT_CLAIMS` (new; was: none; is: empty, so every statement is unchecked until the register is committed): `ref -> {h, cl, by, note}`,
  `h` the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-1 of the statement's normalised text (B1: a 40-character key missed most rewords and would have copied
  five overclaim hits into a guarded declaration), `by` the readings, each with its source (a key of `APPEARANCE_SOURCES`, the one table of
  works read), its locator and its reading id in a register; no quotation in the build (the register holds them).
- The guard: `tools/visual/data-invariance.js` has a group "narrative claims (roadmap step 4)"; `test.js`'s file lists (the duplicate-key
  check, the guard's reach: "the five data files"), `css-test.js`'s glyph coverage and `redteam.js`'s retired claims read `narrative.js`; the
  overclaim scan reads it through `build.py`'s list. `test.js` holds the claims: every entry a live statement whose hash matches, a claim word,
  every source in `APPEARANCE_SOURCES`, every reading id a heading of a register whose source is the one named, "fact" and "attributed" on a
  reading made here (never on a citation alone, B4), "disputed" with two sides read, "uncertain" naming its search, no clock time in a note
  (the hours stay the tracks' timings, held by check:chronology); and the inventory current (the review's I11). Each rule shown failing on a
  mutation (a wrong hash, a fact without a reading, a reading of another source, an unknown source, no locator, an unknown reading id, a
  timed note, an unknown statement, a stale inventory: nine errors, then none when restored).
- `check:data` (expected until the reference moves): "CHANGED narrative claims (roadmap step 4): 2 declarations ... not found: CLAIM_WORDS,
  STATEMENT_CLAIMS"; every other group identical (128 declarations).
- **The review of `f40ea90`, and what changed for it.** (1) The drift hash covered a pair's text but not its label (a timeline line's clock,
  a place fact's name, a Command row's kind and source grade, a layer's name: 125 of the 687 statements), so a retimed line or a regraded row
  kept its claim: `statements()` now returns `whole` (label and text) and the hash is of it. (2) A malformed entry (`by` a string, a null
  entry or reading) crashed `test.js` in the inventory before its errors printed: `inventory.js` never throws on one, and `test.js` reports
  "not an object" / "by is not a list" and builds the inventory inside a try. (3) Three rules were weaker than their words: "disputed" now
  needs two sides read from two sources (one reading used twice passed); "uncertain" needs the sources searched, each with its locator (a
  note alone passed); "fact" needs a reading the register labels fact and read on a page image (an OCR-only entry passed), "attributed" a
  reading read on a page image; the register parser reads each entry's label and whether it was read on the text layer alone. (4) The clock-time
  net in a note missed "a quarter to nine", "half-past eight", "at about nine", "the eighth hour", "nine in the morning", "9 a.m.", "14h30",
  "1400 hours" and the curly apostrophe, and hit "1.25 km": widened and narrowed (26 time forms caught, 18 non-times passed, run). (5) The
  register parser kept a section's source across any other "##" heading: every "##" heading now ends a section, and a reading with no
  source fails. (6) A claim's source counted as "cited nowhere" in the appearance checks: a claim now counts. (7) Prototype keys
  (`constructor`) passed as sources, and unknown fields (a `q` quotation, a typo) passed: own keys only, and a claim is `{h, cl, by, note}`,
  a reading `{src, at, rd, side}`. (8) Records: the guard's comment ("four data files"), `tools/audit/size.js`'s file list. Recorded, not
  changed: the step-2 register's §2.3 and §2.6 also read the French Stutterheim (`stutterheim1806fr`) but resolve to the German key (their
  section's); and `check:data` exits 1 by design until the reference moves, so the draft PR's CI stops at it (it runs before
  check:chronology in `.github/workflows/checks.yml`) for the rest of the step. Each tightened rule shown failing on a mutation (14 errors
  from seven mutated entries, then none when restored).

## 2026-10 · Roadmap step 3: accessibility and robustness (decisions 133, 134; A-1 to A-3, SW-1 to SW-12, S-1 to S-3, S-6)

**Status: merged (#51); the screen-reader session recorded complete on the owner's word on 14 October 2026 (decision 175; recorded in
roadmap step 4's first commit), so step 3 is done. The build changed: `austerlitz-command-map.html` 2,048,277 bytes, md5 `f023ae0e425653deced975402b4cdea7` (was the step-2 build, 1,927,346
bytes, md5 `af98f58641a29cb4934ca9d28bf86071`).** `check:baseline` moves to this build. `check:data`'s reference is not moved: step 3 is
presentation and software only, and no guarded declaration changed (all 128 identical to `archive/step2-af98f586.html`, run after every
code commit). The next owner decision is 176: this step put questions 162-175 to the owner (below), each with the conservative default
implemented meanwhile; the owner decided all as recommended on 11 October 2026, applied after the answers (below), with two answers asked
for on the way: `narrow-1024`'s unobstructed baseline re-measured once for the Panels button (the one limit step 3 moves,
[0.535, 0.628] to [0.533, 0.628]), and decision 174's reading kept in the dispatch card where the caption cannot hold it whole.

**How it was done.** The step's plan (not committed): the current state read from the code, then a design workflow (one designer per
cluster, each proposal challenged by an implementation skeptic and an accessibility skeptic, then a synthesizer and a completeness critic).
The commits, in order: the records `a054554`; C1 `118a288`, C2 `64e70dd`, C3 `864c3d3`, their review fixes `390bfbc`; C4 `f96fc6d`, C5
`cdb932d`, C6 `6e5f571`, C7 `e20bb53`, C8 `4869db5`, C9 `e6d313b`, C10 `a491fca`, C11 `443b657`, the review fixes of C4-C6 `656cf7d`; C12
`ad3c596`, C13 `450cbe5`, C14 `0dc8963`, the report-diff tool `60612c2`; the review fixes of C7-C14 `5593ceb`; C15-C16 `d5a28f3`, C18
`146453d`, C19 and C22 `ce64ed0`, C20-C21 `a3662c9`, C23 `c9facbe`; the review fixes of the five commits `5593ceb`-`a3662c9`, `7736731`; the caption's tag measure
`11d10c5`; the review fix of the map layer's topmost probe `99733eb`; the manifest `fd3d9b1`; the records, part 1, `652a4f8`; the review fixes of `7736731`-`fd3d9b1` `191ab98`; the manifest again `0e2b348`; the records, part 2 (this entry), part 3 `8550689` (the final check:visual) and the records' review fixes. Each segment was reviewed by independent reviewers before the next; every finding is fixed in its "review fixes"
commit or recorded here. The plan's C17 (the phases taking the acts' clicks) waits on question 166 and was not built.

**What changed, by finding.**
- **SW-1, decision 133 (a): three.js and the start (C5, C6).** three.js stays on cdnjs r128; its tag carries
  `integrity="sha512-dLxUel…"`, `crossorigin="anonymous"` and `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` (cdnjs's own form; `node_modules/three`
  0.128.0 is byte-identical to cdnjs's file: 603,445 bytes, the same sha384 and sha512, fetched and compared in this session). An inline
  start-up guard (`AUS_BOOT`, ES5, before the tag): until the first frame, a failed or mismatched three.js, no WebGL, or any uncaught error
  shows `#boot-fail`, an alert dialog with its reason, focus on Reload kept there, everything else inert, no key reaching the app; after 20 s
  without a frame a status line, "Still loading the 3D view…" (never a failure). A lost graphics context shows `#glnotice` (an alert with
  Reload) and stops the frames; restored, they go on. The words are question 162's; the raw error goes to the console only. The tools serve
  three.js one way (`tools/visual/three-route.js`), check the page's integrity against the routed copy, and report a failed start at once.
- **SW-2, SW-3: the narrow layout and the hidden panels (C11, C12).** The closed dossier is `visibility:hidden` after its slide and inert;
  the hidden rail too; one writer of `inert` from its reasons (`syncInert`). Below 1080 px a rail shown (Esc after Watch or Clean) stands
  beside the dispatch card, never over it; at 720 px and below the card gives way to it. A departure from the audit's fix sentence, stated:
  it also had `showEverything` show the rail only from 1080 px, which would leave the order of battle, the analysis, command and plans tabs
  and the only Sources button out of reach below 1080 px (question 164 asks for a visible control instead).
- **SW-4, SW-6: the two sheets as modal dialogs (C9).** The sources sheet and the "?" overlay (`SHEETS`): focus moved in, kept in by Tab,
  returned to the opener; the rest inert but the live regions; no key acting behind; Esc closes the topmost sheet first and no longer clears
  the chapter and the selection; the scrim closes the sources sheet; a click on the text keeps the keys (SW-6).
- **SW-5, SW-9, SW-12: focus where a control disappears (C7, C8, C11, C19).** `shown()` and `focusTo()`: the tour's ways out, the Layers
  panel, the chip, the sightlines' Clear, the presentation switch, the dossier (focus to its opener; a rebuild keeps it), a map item that
  leaves the map (the next stop, else the layer). The Layers panel closes with Watch and Clean (SW-9). A click alone (a screen reader's,
  speech input's) ends the opening and closes the first card as a press does (SW-12, generalised).
- **SW-7: the effects (C2).** `initFX` builds its targets and materials once (`FX.built`); off and on again reuses them (the audit measured
  6 textures added per cycle); a set that fails is disposed.
- **SW-8: the wheel (C3).** A mostly sideways wheel changes nothing; a wheel over the map closes the first card, then zooms.
- **SW-10: layout seams (C13).** The narrow layout at `max-width:1079.98px` (exactly 1080 px was both); the pixel ratio followed on
  resize and on a change of screen density; the `@media` rules that never applied (the 430 px-tall block's three `#firstrun` rules and
  the 360 px-tall block's) moved after the rules they override, the 720 px block's two redundant `#firstrun` declarations removed.
- **SW-11: the reading during the opening and the tour (C21).** Both set the visitor's "Whose eyes?" reading aside (everyone's) and give it
  back on every way out, unless the visitor chose one meanwhile (`TOURCV`). Silently: question 171.
- **S-1: corps counters under "Whose eyes?" (C20; handed on by step 1).** A corps or column counter is its formations' reading
  (`aggReading`): not drawn when none of its formations on the field is known; else at the mean of the known ones, "reported only" when none
  is seen, its grade the worst of theirs, no strength while only some are known (question 170 (a)).
- **S-2: the dwell toggle (C1).** Off and on while the clock plays never sends it back (`dwellSet`, `dwellReset`).
- **S-3 and the eye-level floor (C4; handed on by step 1).** A phase's camera leaves the eye level; leaving it lifts the eye with the floor
  before any frame, so the render-time guard no longer corrects and warns. `CONSOLE_ALLOW` is empty (its one entry, `eye-leave-floor`, was
  removed in the same commit).
- **S-6: reduced motion (C14).** `RM` follows its media query live (what moves stops where it would end); the stylesheet turns every
  transition and animation off under the preference.
- **A-1, decision 134 (a): single-key shortcuts (C10).** A "Single-key shortcuts" switch in the "?" overlay, on by default, for the session
  only (nothing stored, decision 117); off, no key that types one character acts outside text fields, ends the opening or closes the card;
  Space, the arrows, Esc, Tab and Enter keep their rules (question 169).
- **A-2: a focused map item always drawn (C19).** The keyboard focus takes no part in the layout: the focused item keeps its place, or,
  dropped or behind the ground, is drawn over the others at its anchor, clear of the panels where a place beside it is free. Recorded: a
  focused counter keeps its compact form (the full one is the selection's and the hover's; its accessible name carries what the full one
  shows), so that nothing else moves when the focus does. A click alone on an item selects it.
- **A-3: target sizes (C15, C16).** The time rail and the event markers' row 24 px (the track 53 to 55 px; the timeline's height
  unchanged), the panels' close and back buttons, the Sources button, the Layers close and the scope's clear at least 24 px. Events that
  start at the same minute list one another in their dossiers ("Starting at the same minute"), so each has a pointer path. The acts
  (15 px) and the phases (16 px), left below 24 px until the owner's answer, are taken in D5 (decision 166 (a), below); the event markers
  (8 px drawn, a 20 px hit area) are 2.5.8's essential exception (decision 167).
- **Decision 159: the Watch caption (C18; handed on by step 2).** Measured against `#tb-cap`'s box: where the caption shows the derived
  readings (Watch, and Study with the dispatch hidden) they stand before the event names; the act, the phase's title and the event names
  shrink first, and what still cannot fit gives way whole (`fitCaption`: the reading's emphasis, then the later reading, then the events)
  instead of an ellipsis through a reading. The order and the fit follow the presentation, the dispatch and the "Eyes" button at once.
  `measure.js` `capDerived` is now "shown, inside the box and not ellipsized".
- **The narrow layout's event tag (handed on by step 2).** The caption's tag never shrinks (its name does; the event gives way whole where
  even its tag cannot stand); `measure.js` `capTag`, judged in every view.
- **An event's map label carries its note (C22; handed on by step 2).** "(hour disputed)", "(interval)", "(reconstruction)", in the
  caption tag's short words (`evMapText`, `LABELS.event.map`; "hour disputed", not the arrows' bare "(disputed)": the class disputes an
  hour, not the event); its accessible name begins with its drawn words (WCAG 2.5.3).
- **`pickFormation` on every pointer move (C23; handed on by step 1).** Measured, `tools/step3/hover-cost.js`, rule set before measuring:
  a fix only if a move's p95 exceeds 2 ms. On the build of `99733eb` (the hover's path is unchanged since), at 1600 x 900 under software WebGL, 400 moves over the free part of the screen in each of five views (`overview-field`, `close-sokolnitz`, `hybrid-dimmed`, `paper-north-up`, `pratzen-low-10x`), with the evidence skeleton off and on, each timed three times: the median at most 0.1 ms, the worst p95 0.4 ms (`pratzen-low-10x`, skeleton on), the worst move 1.0 ms. No fix is called for. (Chromium rounds `performance.now()` to 0.1 ms, so the medians are at its resolution.)

**A finding of the step, recorded.** Under software WebGL (the harness's SwiftShader), turning the effects off and on recompiles every
shader at the next frame and the frames after it slow to about 9 s each; the same happens on the step-2 build. The first SW-7 check drew a
frame after each toggle and so stalled the real-key checks after it; it now counts the builds and the render targets made (`FX.builds`,
`FX.rts`) without drawing. Whether a GPU shows the stall is not measured.

T-4, T-5, with T-3 and T-6, before any data task) and 132 (CI). Choices made within decision 141, stated for the owner: the sans is Inter
4.001, renamed "Austerlitz Sans" (SIL Open Font License 1.1), with one glyph, U+2502 (the timeline's event buttons), from DejaVu Sans 2.37
(Bitstream Vera and Arev licences) as a second face of the family; the serif is TeX Gyre Pagella 2.501, renamed "Austerlitz Serif" (GUST
Font License, an instance of the LPPL 1.3c or later); each renamed as its licence asks. The re-measure takes `--bounds keep`: a limit
changes only where the fonts moved the measure past it, rather than every limit set to its count by decision 62's method, which would leave
no slack for step 2's longer plateau label (decision 126's trade-off).
